resources.string: Fetching the hour-by-hour forecast for where you are.
Check your connection and pull to try again.
Allow location access so the app can read the UV forecast for your exact spot. Nothing leaves your phone except the coordinates sent to the weather service.
No stretch of daylight stays under UV %1$d today.
Time outside if you take every window
That uses %1$s of what it would take to pink your skin — no burn, and only a small amount of the slow kind of exposure.
Taking all of it would pass your pink threshold. Break it up, or take the gentlest window only.
Remind me when a window opens
Tells you when a gentle stretch of daylight opens.
Gentle until %1$s. UV is low enough to stay out the whole window.
Gentle until %1$s. Your skin would take about %2$s to start pinking.

The number that matters. Each window shows how long you could stay before your skin would just start to pink, and the bar shows how much of that allowance the day\'s windows use up. Staying well inside it means no burn, and the ultraviolet you do collect is the small, slow kind — which is what adds up over decades into ageing.
How windows are picked. The app reads the hourly forecast for your exact spot, cloud cover already included, and marks every stretch of daylight sitting at or under your limit.

Honest caveat. No amount of ultraviolet is completely free of risk — the risk falls smoothly as UV falls but never reaches zero. This finds the gentlest daylight of your day. It is not medical advice.
